rationale: uswin-claude-agentic: train_n=579, val_n=214, epochs=21, batch_size=4, lr=0.0005, uswin_c=24, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=970, seed=42, rationale=ITER-6 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). START FROM iter-5 BEST (tn480/ep26/c24, hr 0.3829, #2 on the Mayo board). ONE KNOB: TRAINING DATA train_n 480 -> 579 (FULL 579-slice pool, 100pct coverage), with epochs TRADED DOWN 26 -> 21 to fit the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall. uswin_c stays 24 (iter-3/5 best), all else identical to iter-5 (val_n=214, bs=4, lr=5e-4, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) TRAJECTORY iter-1 ep10/tn200 -> hr 0.173021 in 328.96s; iter-2 ep40/tn200 -> 0.322063 in 737.72s; iter-3 ep64/tn200 -> 0.353196 in 1085.87s; iter-4 c32/ep34/tn200 REGRESSED -> 0.272533 in 760.76s (capacity-for-epochs trade FAILED); iter-5 tn480/ep26/c24 -> 0.382872 / SSIM 0.921690 / PSNR 38.27 in 1154.72s (CURRENT BEST, #2 on the Mayo board). best hr = 0.382872 @iter-5. (2) LIMITER: the DATA-COVERAGE lever just delivered uswin biggest single jump (+0.0297, 0.3532->0.3829) DESPITE trading epochs 64->26 -- coverage DOMINATED the epoch loss, so the binding constraint is the LAST 17pct of the train pool, NOT epochs. iter-5 trained on 480/579 = 82.9pct coverage; the remaining 99 distinct slices (480->579) are data the net has NEVER seen. The champion dual_domain_supervised went all the way to train_n=579 (full pool) to hit 0.3994 -- the proven path. Epoch-starvation at ep26 is the WEAKER hypothesis (the data jump worked despite fewer epochs). solver_uswin.py does NOT use RotatingSubsetDataset -- build_dataset calls load_val_split once for a FIXED train_n set and reshuffles the SAME samples every epoch via torch.randperm, so train_n IS load-bearing: tn579 loads strictly MORE distinct slices (the full 154+98+327 = 579 pool spanning all 3 ps-groups / 4 train patients). (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 480->579 (epochs 26->21 is a forced budget-trade, not a second free knob; c stays iter-5 24). BUDGET-TRADE MATH (worst-case-sized): iter-5 exact calibration: per_sample_epoch = (1154.72-157)/(26*480) = 0.07995 s/sample-epoch (matches iter-5 worst-case 0.07981 estimate -> calibration exact); fixed (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure I/O, train_n-independent since val fixed at 214) = 157s. At tn579 per_epoch = 579*0.07995 = 46.3 s/epoch. ep21 = 157 + 21*46.3 = 1129s = 18.8 min (71s margin inside 1200s); ep22 = 1175s = 19.6 min (only 25s margin -> too tight given iter-5 already ran hot to 1154.72s), so ep21 is the LARGEST epoch count guaranteed to fit. Train-only = 21*46.3 = 972s; max_train_s=970 set as the HARD train-only backstop so even at hot per-sample cost train halts <=970s leaving >=230s for the worst-case 214-slice val+figure inside the 1200s budget. (4) HYPOTHESIS: the final 17pct of the train pool (480->579 distinct slices, completing the full pool exactly as the champion did) lifts hr above the iter-5 0.382872, because uswin hr rose monotonically with coverage (200->480 gained +0.0297) and the champion proved 480->579 is worth ~0.015-0.02 headroom. Predicted iter-6 hr ~0.39-0.40. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.382872 at tn579/ep21, uswin is at its budget-constrained ceiling (~0.383) -- the last data slug could not overcome the ep26->21 trade -- and it stays #2 behind dual_domain_supervised (0.3994). (5) HARD 20-min train+score budget; val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices (NOT reduced); grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP, bg_target=truth, metric=321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). (6) no control return.
